title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

reading.body:
Waymo autonomous vehicles became stranded in heavy traffic near the Golden Gate Bridge during Fourth of July celebrations when their batteries drained faster than expected in gridlocked conditions. At least a dozen vehicles, primarily Jaguar I-PACE models, stopped on city streets while carrying no operators. One vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks debris, though no injuries resulted.

The deployment of autonomous vehicles without operator presence created a failure mode where the system could not adapt to or escape extended congestion. The vehicles were used in conditions their battery capacity was not designed to sustain, and there was no fallback mechanism to move stalled vehicles or prevent them from obstructing traffic. A system that could have monitored battery depletion in real time against predicted traffic patterns and either rerouted vehicles away from the event or recalled them before gridlock might have prevented the stranding.

It is not established whether Waymo had prior warning of the traffic conditions or whether the route planning system failed to account for holiday congestion in this area.

reports.title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

summary:
During Fourth of July celebrations in San Francisco on Saturday, multiple Waymo autonomous vehicles became stranded in heavy traffic after their batteries drained. NBC News verified video footage showing at least a dozen stationary Waymo vehicles, primarily Jaguar I-PACE models, lined up on streets near the Golden Gate Bridge fireworks display. One vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks, though no injuries were reported. The company attributed the gridlock to major traffic disruptions, high traveler volume, and unexpected road closures, stating that its roadside assistance team worked to clear the vehicles.

The incident caused significant frustration among drivers stuck in standstill traffic for hours. Some witnesses reported frustration about driverless cars with no operators present during the congestion. Mayor Daniel Lurie's office indicated it would meet with stakeholders to improve traffic management for future events. This incident follows a December outage when over 100,000 customers lost power and some Waymo vehicles stopped at intersections with non-functioning traffic lights, highlighting challenges the autonomous vehicle service faces during major disruptions.
